newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: "Last weld" complete on Colombia's Ocensa pipeline.
newsitem.headline: "Last weld" complete on Colombia's Ocensa pipeline.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc said Friday the "last weld" had now been completed on Colombia's 500 mile (800 km) Ocensa pipeline -- the largest in the country.

Crude from the Cusiana-Cupiagua field, in eastern Casanare province, operated by BP's Colombian unit BP Exploration (BPX), will begin to be pumped along the completed pipeline at the end of this month or early next, unit president John Doust said in a Reuter interview.
"This is the symbolic beginning of what's been a world-class engineering construction feat across the Andes," he said.

The completion of the pipework along the Ocensa line in fact marks the end of the second stage of the $2 billion project, in which BPX has a 15 percent stake, alongside state-run oil company Ecopetrol, Total Pipeline Colombie and Triton Pipeline Colombia.

About 185,000 barrels per day of Cusiana mix and another 100,000 barrels per day from the Apiay field, in the central Magdalena Medio region, have been pumped along some of the completed sections of the Ocensa pipeline for the last several months.

In areas where the pipeline was not finished, crude was diverted through temporary pipework and along part of the Colombia pipeline -- until now the country's second largest operational pipeline after Cano Limon-Covenas -- to the lifting terminal at the Caribbean coast port of Covenas.
Doust said that by the end of July or early August the Ocensa pipeline would be handling a total of about 450,000 barrels of crude per day -- about 320,000 of that from the Cusiana field.

That total will rise to a maximum of some 620,000 barrels per day when production increases to about 500,000 barrels per day in the Cusiana-Cupiagua field at the end of December or early January 1998, Doust said.

In order to allow Ocensa to operate at full capacity, work is still being carried out to complete a series of new pumping stations. The pipeline, which has taken 25 million man-hours to complete, runs from Cusiana-Cupiagua to Covenas, crossing mountain ranges as high as 10,000 feet and gradients of between 60 and 70 percent.
Doust has described the construction of Ocensa as "technically as challenging" as the Transalaska pipeline.

Previously Colombia's largest pipeline was the one that runs from Occidental Petroleum Corp's field at Cao Limon in eastern Arauca province to Covenas, with a capacity of about 200,000 barrels per day.
